messages:
mira: Hey team — customer (acme-corp) escalated: streaming responses truncate after ~65s of silence, client reconnects and ends up billed for partial + resumed tokens. Started right after we rotated API keys for their org yesterday.
sam: Ouch. Do we have the request id / example request headers from them?
mira: They sent req id req_8Gf3w4. Headers they pasted:

Authorization: Bearer <token-redacted>
User-Agent: AcmeClient/2.1
Accept: text/event-stream

Repro curl they ran (they used golang client but this is minimal):
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \  
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \  
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-xl"
```
They say connection is closed by network after ~65s, then client reconnects and gets duplicate prefix + different continuation. Also they observed a 401 mid-stream once during a reconnect.
alex: Two likely interacting things: 1) ALB (and some LBs) have default idle timeout 60s — if no bytes go across for that window, LB will reset connection. 2) If token rotation/refresh happens server-side and we return a 401 on a reconnect or during a revalidation handshake, client can see mid-stream auth failure. Combined -> truncated chunk + reconnect loop. Also Cloudflare/edge accelerators can rebuffer and present partial chunk boundaries differently than origin.
nina: Can we get envoy/origin logs for req_8Gf3w4? Specifically need downstream FIN/RST from ALB or 502/503 from upstream. Also want TCP close events from the load balancer side.
mira: Pasted partial proxy logs from the customer side (they captured headers and saw a RST after 65s):
```
[2026-02-21T12:04:05Z] conn_id=1132 recv_bytes=0 idle_timeout=60 -> FIN
[2026-02-21T12:05:10Z] upstream resp partial: chunked, bytes=4096, closed by peer
```
support-bot: deploy-bot: rotated customer org key for acme-corp at 3612339500 (rotation id rot_2026_02_21_16).

sam: That rotation timestamp is ~1h before these reports — could be correlated. If the client retried and presented old token it would get 401; but 401 mid-stream is odd unless we terminate with HTTP status on reconnect. We should also check our streaming gateway behavior on token expiry: do we gracefully close with an event or immediate 401?
alex: Immediate mitigation steps: 1) ask customer to enable a heartbeat every 20s (send `
` or an SSE comment `: keepalive

`) so LB sees traffic and won't idle-close. 2) As a platform we can add a default keepalive ping every 15s from gateway when upstream silence >15s (config change). 3) For ALB specifically, bump idle timeout to 300s if acceptable for their infra.
nina: Longer term: ensure token rotation uses a short grace window for live streams — if token used at start rotates mid-stream, we should accept or allow a refresh handshake to continue the stream rather than issuing 401 that terminates it.
mira: Customer asked for repro steps we can run from our side. I'll try a quick repro from a VM in us-east-1 hitting through ALB with a 60s idle probe to simulate. Reproducer command I'm going to run:```
# simulate slow token-exchange + silent server
socat -u TCP-LISTEN:9000,reuseaddr,fork SYSTEM:'printf "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: text/event-stream\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n\r\n4\r\ndata\r\n0\r\n"; sleep 70; printf "4\r\nmore\r\n0\r\n"' &

curl -N http://<alb>/proxy-to-socat
```

sam: Nice. Capture tcpdump on client-facing side and ALB logs. Also capture x-forwarded-for and x-amzn-trace-id. If we see LB FIN at ~60s with no bytes after, that's confirmed.
alex: For customer-side quick workaround advise: 1) enable streaming heartbeats from client; 2) set ALB idle timeout >= 120s; 3) if behind Cloudflare, enable "origin keepalive"/disable HTTP/2 connection coalescing for SSE paths.
mira: I've emailed the customer those workarounds and asked for full proxy logs + pcap. I've also opened an internal ENG issue and tagged eng-runtime for token-grace behavior: https://redwood.internal/issue/INF-6523
nina: Assigned to eng-runtime with high priority. Please attach the repro pcap and the exact rotation id rot_2026_02_21_16 so they can correlate key handling.
support-bot: incident-bot: created incident INC-2026-183 (streaming-truncation-acme) with Sev=2, linked rotation rot_2026_02_21_16.
mira: I'll follow up with a timeline and customer's billing concern (they were charged for both partial and resumed tokens). Sam, can you draft a billing credit note template? :pray:
sam: On it, mir a. Drafted refund template and will send after we confirm root cause. :thumbsup:
mira: Thanks — will update thread after repro run.
